recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say what you divide by and which two standard limits you then use.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Divide above and below by x
steps.margin_note: First mark. Both parts are 0 at x = 0, so neither is a standard limit on its own. Dividing both by x makes each one a standard limit.
lines: At x = 0, eˣ − 1 = 0 and √(1 + x) − 1 = 0, so the expression is of the indeterminate form 0/0.
For x ≠ 0 divide the numerator and the denominator by x.

recall.must_convey: That the numerator and denominator are each divided by x so that both become standard limits.
accept: divide the top and the bottom by x so both become standard limits
both parts go to zero so divide each by x
use e to the x minus one over x is one and root one plus x minus one over x is half
rendinni x tho divide cheste standard limits vasthayi
split it into two standard limits by dividing by x
heard_as: e to the x minus one

steps.why: The denominator is also 0 at x = 0, so this is a ratio of two 0/0 pieces. Dividing each by x is what turns them into the two standard limits the syllabus states.
common_mistakes: Treating the denominator as a constant and answering 1.
Dividing only the numerator by x and forgetting the denominator.
steps.memory_tip: lim (eˣ − 1)/x = 1 is the a = e case of lim (aˣ − 1)/x = logₑa, because logₑe = 1. One formula, not two.

steps.label: Take the ratio of the two standard limits
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Both limits exist and the lower one, 1/2, is not 0, so the quotient rule applies. Dividing by 1/2 is multiplying by 2.
lines: Both limits exist and the denominator limit 1/2 is not 0, so the limit of the quotient is the quotient of the limits.

recall.must_convey: That the answer is 1 divided by 1/2, that is 2.
accept: one divided by half gives two
dividing by one half multiplies by two

steps.why: The quotient rule for limits needs both limits to exist and the lower one to be non-zero, and both conditions hold here. The value checks numerically: at x = 0.00001 the expression is 2.000015.
common_mistakes: Multiplying by 1/2 instead of dividing by it, giving 1/2.
Giving 1 by using the numerator limit only.
steps.memory_tip: Dividing by 1/2 doubles the number, and the top limit here is 1, so the answer is simply 2.

insider_note: Divide top and bottom by x so both become standard limits, 1 and 1/2. Dividing by a half doubles, so the answer is 2 — the same shape as the 3ˣ version.
